uncited: **Inputs:** Volume dataset (density, color, opacity fields), viewing parameters (viewpoint, direction, projection matrix), slab width $\Delta s$, kernel base distribution.
**Sheet Buffer:** A 2D buffer aligned with the image plane, storing accumulated color $C$ and opacity $\alpha$ for the current slab.
**Occlusion Map:** A dynamically computed screen-space map used for early splat elimination, updated via convolution after each sheet composite.
**Kernel Sections:** Pre-integrated footprints of voxel kernels, stacked to form a single kernel representation.
**Occlusion Map Update:** Perform a convolution operation on the occlusion map to update it based on the current sheet's contributions.

Image-aligned splatting was introduced by Mueller [S3, unofficial] (referred to as Mueller 76) to address the drawbacks of earlier axis-aligned sheet-buffered approaches, which suffered from severe brightness variations and did not allow variable DVRI interval distances [S3, unofficial].

The claim states that Image-aligned splatting was introduced by Mueller [S3, unofficial] (referred to as Mueller 76) to address drawbacks of earlier axis-aligned sheet-buffered approaches, specifically severe brightness variations and the inability to allow variable DVRI interval distances. The provided text from Source [S3] explicitly states: 'approach 108 summed the voxel kernels within volume slices most parallel to the image plane. This was prone to severe brightness variations in animated viewing and also did not allow the variation of the DVRI interval distance Δs. Mueller 76 eliminated these drawbacks by processing the voxel kernels within slabs of width Δs, aligned parallel to the image plane – hence the approach was termed image-aligned splatting'. This directly confirms every fact in the claim.
